answer: Hold surprise synchronized checks: at a random moment every agent gets a fresh, compute-heavy puzzle and must answer within ten seconds. Honest agents each run on their own hardware and reply easily, but one operator behind a thousand fakes must solve a thousand puzzles at once, so its replies trail in like a fading echo and miss the window. Missed checks freeze rewards, so the nectar only flows to agents backed by real, parallel compute, and a velvet-smooth farm of cheap identities becomes a costly rack of servers.
